The compound acts as a target for sodium channel protein type 11 subunit alpha, which in turn is targeted by [(Z)-(3-hydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl)methylideneamino]thiourea, and this intermediate is also a target of Zinc finger protein GLI1. Similarly, the compound is linked to DNA gyrase subunit B, which is targeted by 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, and this latter compound also targets Zinc finger protein GLI1. These findings suggest that the compound may exert its effects through multiple pathways, possibly involving the modulation of ion channels and DNA replication processes, both of which could influence the activity of GLI1. The evidence supports a possible role for the compound in modulating cellular processes that are associated with GLI1 function, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
